chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a woman who cut off the breast of her bondwoman that she is free, and her mistress has no authority over her. And he ruled that whoever mutilates his slave, then he is free, and he has no authority over him; he is set free, going and affiliating himself with whomever he wishes, and if someone guarantees his liability, then he inherits from him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام in his role as the authoritative judge and leader
key_terms.جَرِيرَتَهُ: his liability or legal responsibility for wrongdoing
key_terms.سَائِبَةٌ: a freed person left unattached and at liberty
key_terms.قَضَى: issued a legal judgment or ruling
key_terms.نَكَّلَ: inflicted mutilation or severe punitive harm

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a master mutilates or severely harms a slave in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports legal rulings of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning the emancipation of a slave subjected to severe bodily harm or mutilation by the owner. It also states that such a freed person may attach himself by wala' to whomever he wishes, and inheritance follows when someone assumes liability for his legal obligations.
